name: validator-f9944c58-blind30
instr:
# Repairing go-playground/validator without a test suite

The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything that has been noticed from the outside, written in terms of what was done and what came back.

This library is used to attach rules to the fields of a record type, ask for a value to be examined against them, and turn whatever failed into messages a person can read. Nothing about how it is called changed, and nothing about the rules being asked for changed. The same programs that used to get correct answers now get wrong ones: verdicts reached the wrong way round, breakage that goes unreported, and reports that come back missing pieces or in the wrong words.

Start with the plainest thing a caller does, which is hand over a value and ask whether it passes. A rule that demands a field differ from the matching field of a companion record now answers backwards for unsigned whole numbers: two equal values are accepted, and values that differ are flagged. The same rule on text, signed numbers, floats, booleans, lists, timestamps and durations still gives the answers it always gave. A rule argument that itself contains an equals sign is now cut short at that sign, so asking that a value exclude every character in the set written as `!@#$%^&*()_+.0x2C=?` no longer excludes `=` and a lone `=` sails through, while the same rule with an argument holding no second equals sign, such as a set of brackets and punctuation, is still read whole and s
